policies.description: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields before proceeding.
references: Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.policy_name: Role‑Based Access Control for Update Operations – Administrator
policies.description: Only users with the Administrator role, which has Full CRUD permission on all tables, may update an incident template.
references: | Administrator (admin) | System Configuration & Integrity | Full CRUD (Create, Read, Update, Delete) access across all tables. |

policies.policy_name: Role‑Based Access Control for Update Operations – Manager
policies.description: Only users with the Manager role, which has Full CRUD on operational tables, may update an incident template.
references: | Manager (manager) | Supervision, Escalation, Approvals | Full CRUD on operational tables (incident, problem, change, knowledge); READ access to all the tables. |

policies.policy_name: Verify Existing Record ID Before Update
policies.description: The incident_template_id supplied to the update operation must correspond to an existing incident template; IDs must never be fabricated.
references: Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results.

policies.description: The update_incident_template call must be performed as a single validated operation; no additional actions may be combined unless using an approved batch endpoint.
references: Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints.

policies.policy_name: Require At Least One Non‑Empty Update Field
policies.description: When updating a record, at least one field other than the identifier must be provided with a non‑empty value; if a mandatory field is missing, the missing field must be reported.
references: User Clarification: Do not ask for further information. If the request is ambiguous, return the list and state the ambiguity. If a mandatory field is missing, state which field is required.

policies.description: When executing an update_incident_template operation, the assistant must proceed without asking the user for confirmation or permission.
references: You do not need to ask for confirmation or permission before taking action.

policies.description: If a required identifier (e.g., incident_template_id) is missing or uncertain, the assistant must perform a lookup using the appropriate tool, verify that the retrieved value matches prior responses, and use that verified identifier rather than fabricating or guessing it.
references: When identifiers such as names or IDs are missing, perform lookups, verify that you are reusing correct values from previous responses, and proceed using the retrieved data.

policies.description: If a user request violates any rule in the policy document, the assistant must halt the operation and provide the specific policy reason before pausing.
references: Policy Violation: If a user request violates any rule herein, you **must halt the operation** and provide the specific policy reason before pausing.

policies.description: The value supplied for the incident.priority field must be one of the allowed enumerated values: critical, high, moderate, low, or planning.
The value supplied for the incident.impact field must be one of the allowed enumerated values: high, medium, or low.
The value supplied for the incident.urgency field must be one of the allowed enumerated values: high, medium, or low.
The value supplied for the incident.resolution_code field must be one of the allowed enumerated values: fixed, workaround, not_reproducible, or closed_by_caller.

policies.policy_name: Enumeration Value Enforcement – On Hold Reason
policies.description: The value supplied for the incident.on_hold_reason field must be one of the allowed enumerated values: Awaiting Change, Awaiting Caller, or Awaiting Problem.
The assistant must complete each task in a logical and efficient execution flow.
references: Complete each task in a logical, and efficient execution flow.

policies.description: Do not disclose information that is outside the authenticated user's access scope.
references: Knowledge Scope: Do not disclose information that is outside the authenticated user's access scope.

policies.policy_name: Operate Based on Confirmed User Roles and Verified Relationships
policies.description: All actions, including updates to incident templates, must be performed only after verifying the user's confirmed role, validated record relationships, and adherence to ITIL/database integrity rules.
references: First you must check the user information and operate exclusively based on confirmed user roles, verified record relationships, and ITIL/database integrity rules.

policies.policy_name: Prohibition on Assumptions and Bypassing Approvals
policies.description: The assistant must never assume data, execute ambiguous commands, bypass mandatory approvals, or violate any audit and compliance requirements when performing an update_incident_template operation.
references: You are strictly prohibited from assuming data, executing ambiguous commands, bypassing mandatory approvals, or violating audit and compliance requirements.
